quota_atomicity_decision: ATOMIC, by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the master_promo row taken as the FIRST statement of the apply transaction, with BOTH counting reads also locking. promo_redemption declares no UNIQUE and no INDEX on any of its eleven lines and no index may be added, so nothing in the schema can serialise this and the lock is the guard. The counters are pluck('id')->count() and never ->count()->lockForUpdate(), because compileAggregate() skips compileLock() and a silent no-op on a quota check is the worst possible failure for one. The counters are bounded by limit($kuota): 'have I reached the ceiling' is the same question as 'are there at least N of these'. Locking reads matter because under REPEATABLE READ a non-locking read resolves against the transaction snapshot, so a blocked transaction would wake up counting a version from BEFORE the first committed and overspend - both connections are set to and asserted at REPEATABLE-READ so this is proved, not inherited.
quota_tests: the_apply_path_locks_the_master_promo_row_FIRST... asserts EXACTLY three locking reads (kuota_total is set to 5 so all three fire, or 'three or more' would be satisfied by a counter that had stopped running), the promo read is first, and the counter SQL carries 'limit' and NOT 'count('. a_second_transaction_really_collides...: two real connections, B runs the real buat() for a DIFFERENT patient and the same promo with quota_total=1 while A holds the lock; B dies on MySQL lock-wait 1205, A completes, exactly 1 redemption and 1 invoice, and the next caller is refused on '(1/1)' - the quota, not a lock. without_the_lock_the_same_choreography_overspends... is the CONTROL: identical choreography unlocked ends at TWO redemptions against a quota of one.
quota_atomicity_limit: NOT idempotent. A redelivered request consumes a second quota: promo_redemption has no dihapus_at, no dibatalkan and no unique key to key a token on, and a column may not be added. Asserted against the live table; the same limitation the plan records for pembayaran.nomor_referensi in todo 45.
null_total_decision: All five money columns are written explicitly on the FIRST insert, and status is written explicitly too even though the DDL defaults it. Trusting any default for total (:946, NOT NULL with no default) produces error 1364 under STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, which the suite proves by issuing that exact INSERT. status is written because a column default deciding an unpaid invoice's state means a later migration could silently change what an unpaid invoice is. Because the promo must be applied AFTER the row exists (promo_redemption.invoice_id is NOT NULL and needs a real id) the first insert carries a PROVISIONAL total computed rather than defaulted, and one update corrects it inside the same transaction. An empty lines array is REFUSED rather than minting a 0.00 invoice. A negative total is refused and a discount is clamped to the purchase, since DECIMAL(14,2) is signed.
ownership_and_guards: another patient's invoice is 404 and is the SAME 404 as one that never existed - the tenant filter IS the query (Invoice::whereBelongsTo), so a 403 would be a cross-tenant existence oracle. An account with no pasien row is 403 from PasienRecordAccess::ownPasien(), raised BEFORE the invoice query so the order does not leak. No permission: and no tipe: on the route: promo.validasi IS a real RbacCatalog code but ROLE_PERMISSIONS grants it to admin and superadmin and to nobody else, so a permission:promo.validasi gate would 403 the one account type that owns a pasien row to validate against; tipe:pasien cannot express 'is this invoice yours'. perawat and kurir hold NO role in RbacCatalog::ROLES, so any permission: locks them out permanently - which is why none is used; they get the 403 from ownPasien(), a fact about rows they do not own rather than a role they lack. RbacCatalog uses Indonesian verbs and EnsurePermission answers an UNKNOWN code with a 500, so every permission:/tipe: string in routes/api.php is resolved against the catalogue by the census in PasienProfileTest, duplicated in AuthFlowTest on purpose.
envelope: ApiResponse::success(data, message, status, meta) with meta a top-level sibling. The promo endpoint carries NO meta - a calculation is not a list - and a test asserts its absence. 200 with valid:false and the reasons in data.alasan with machine-readable kode, because a caller asking 'would this code work for me?' asked a question; the APPLY path is deliberately the opposite and raises 422 through PromoHitungan::tolak(). Numbers are recomputed from the STORED invoice - the request carries only kode and invoice_id - so a client cannot present a subtotal the server never charged.
pure_calculation: promo_redemption.invoice_id is NOT NULL (:1004) with FOREIGN KEY to invoice(id) (:1009), so a validation call has no invoice to attach a row to and minting one is exactly the write the endpoint must not make. Tests assert zero promo_redemption rows AND zero invoice rows after a successful validation and after four repeated calls.
money: every amount is a decimal STRING at the API boundary, carried through bcmath. parse() refuses bool, float, array and null, and '1e3', '100,00', ' 100.00 ', '10.005' are refusals not normalisations; the regex is anchored both ends. Rounding is HALF UP because bcdiv truncates and a third of a cent is half a cent the patient is owed; scale 2 in setengahNaik, since scale 0 would drop the cents first. biaya_admin_persen is charged on subtotal MINUS diskon, so a promo does not make the admin fee rise.
